title: sudo: Run as administrator
body: "sudo" is a term used in Linux and Ubuntu to run commands with administrative privileges. Since regular users cannot freely modify system-wide settings or specific folders, they use "sudo" to run commands with higher privileges when necessary. However, because these privileges are so powerful, a single mistake could corrupt system files. When you see `sudo` while running code or installing a package, you should verify whether the task truly requires administrative privileges and what files or settings it will modify. title: Cache: Temporarily stores frequently used results
body: Caching is a method of temporarily storing frequently used results. Recalculating the same request from scratch or re-making the API call every time takes a long time and increases costs. Therefore, previous results are stored so that when the same request is received, it can be returned quickly. In web apps, file caching, API response caching, and browser caching can all be used. When reading code, while caching helps improve speed and reduce costs, you must also consider the risk of outdated results remaining.
